title: Mixed mock B: an onsite loop

questions.stem: In the system design round, the capital-plan solve can take 40 minutes. Where does it run?

options.text: In a Lambda function, since serverless functions scale with demand
options.says: A Lambda invocation runs for at most 900 seconds; Lambda is glue, never the solve.

options.text: In the API process, since FastAPI runs async handlers in parallel
options.says: The API only answers requests; the solve runs as a separate job.

options.text: In Step Functions itself, since a state machine can wait for hours
options.says: Step Functions waits for the job and catches failures; it does not solve.

options.text: In an AWS Batch job on Fargate, with Step Functions waiting for it
options.says: Right: Batch on Fargate runs the solver container, with a timeout above the solver's limit.

questions.stem: A colleague writes the carry-over cash row as an equation (spend plus carry-out equals budget plus carry-in) and caps each year's carry-out at half its budget. A plan spends 20 of a year's 100. What does the model do with it?

options.text: It is allowed, since the 80 left over is carried to the next year
options.says: The equation forces all 80 into the carry, and the cap allows only 50.

options.text: It is refused, since 80 must be carried and the cap allows only 50
options.says: Right: money that should lapse is forced into the carry, so a feasible plan becomes infeasible.

options.text: It is allowed, since an equation and an inequality allow the same plans
options.says: The page says the equation turns a feasible plan into an infeasible model.

options.text: It is refused, since an equation forbids any carry-over at all
options.says: The equation has a carry term; it forbids lapsing, not carrying.

questions.stem: Two planner overrides cost $300k and $200k of NPV when each is priced alone, by solving with and without it. Finance wants the cost of applying both. What do you do?

options.text: Run the model once with the pair in place, since costs need not add
options.says: Right: four overrides cost $618k one at a time and $927k together in lesson 6.5.6.

options.text: Report the sum of the two, since each cost is what that override takes
options.says: Each cost was measured with the other override absent; together they interact.

options.text: Charge the larger override alone, since it already covers the smaller
options.says: The page says the largest single cost does not stand in for the joint cost; the four together cost more than any one.

options.text: Report less than the sum, since overlapping overrides share a cost
options.says: The page rules out a discount for overlap; in its example the four together cost more than the sum.
